content.value_statement: Hybrid network projects require clear choices across VPN, private links, routing, and redundancy. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical hybrid connectivity design.
actual_capabilities: Compare VPN, Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, and Cloud Interconnect options.
Provide Terraform examples for AWS and Azure VPN gateways.
Outline hub-and-spoke, multi-region, and multi-cloud hybrid patterns.
Recommend BGP routing, route propagation, route filtering, and monitoring checks.
Summarize security, high availability, troubleshooting, and cost optimization practices.
limitations: Does not include complete deployment modules or provider-specific automation scripts.
Uses example addresses and resource names that require replacement.
Does not validate account permissions, quotas, or provider availability.
Provides planning guidance, not live network testing.

use_cases.title: Plan Cloud Connectivity
use_cases.description: Design a resilient connection between a data center and AWS, Azure, or GCP.

use_cases.title: Compare Connection Options
use_cases.description: Choose between VPN and private connectivity using bandwidth, latency, reliability, and cost.

use_cases.title: Review Network Controls
use_cases.description: Check routing, monitoring, encryption, and redundancy decisions before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic VPN
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a site-to-site VPN between our data center and AWS. Include routing, security controls, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare VPN, Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, and Cloud Interconnect for a regulated workload. Recommend one option and explain tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design High Availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a high availability hybrid network pattern for two data centers and two cloud regions. Include BGP, failover, and monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this hybrid cloud network plan for routing risk, single points of failure, security gaps, and cost concerns: [paste plan].

output_examples.input: Plan a moderate-bandwidth connection from one data center to AWS.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: Start with site-to-site VPN, enable dynamic routing, monitor tunnel health, and plan Direct Connect if traffic grows.

output_examples.input: Review a hybrid design that has one VPN tunnel and no route filtering.
output: Add a second tunnel or diverse connection for failover.
Use BGP route filtering to prevent unintended route propagation.
Enable flow logs, tunnel telemetry, and alerting for packet loss and latency.

best_practices: Confirm CIDR ranges, BGP ASNs, bandwidth targets, latency needs, and compliance requirements before selecting a connection.
Design redundancy with dual tunnels, diverse paths, route filtering, and monitored failover.
Replace documentation addresses and names with approved production values before deployment.
anti_patterns: Using example CIDR blocks or public IP addresses in production without review.
Building a single VPN tunnel for workloads that need high availability.
Skipping route filtering, flow logging, or DDoS protection for cross-premises traffic.

faq.question: Which cloud providers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers AWS, Azure, and GCP hybrid connectivity patterns.

faq.question: Does it create production infrastructure automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that require review before deployment.

faq.question: Can it help choose between VPN and private connectivity?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares cost, bandwidth, latency, reliability, and setup effort.

faq.question: Does it include routing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers BGP, route propagation, filtering, and advertised CIDR planning.

faq.question: Can it support high availability planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes dual tunnels, active-active patterns, and failover monitoring.

faq.question: Is it suitable for security reviews?
faq.answer: It can support early review of encryption, logging, endpoints, and network controls.
